about: Justification trainer prompts for Unit 6 (docs/apcalc-architecture.md, "Justification trainer"). Every number is recomputed in scripts/lib/apcalc-exams.mjs (JUSTIFY_NUMBERS).

prompts.title: A left sum with unequal widths
prompts.context:
Water flows into a tank at an increasing rate $r(t)$ liters per minute. Selected values are in the table.

$t$ (minutes)0259
$r(t)$ (L/min)47912
prompts.prompt: Approximate $\int_0^9 r(t)\,dt$ with a left Riemann sum using the three subintervals in the table. Is it an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.
checklist: Gets $2(4) + 3(7) + 4(9) = 65$ liters, with the unit of the accumulated amount
Says it is an underestimate because $r$ is increasing, so each left height is the smallest on its subinterval

earns.answer: $\int_0^9 r(t)\,dt \approx 2 \cdot r(0) + 3 \cdot r(2) + 4 \cdot r(5) = 2(4) + 3(7) + 4(9) = 65$ liters. Since $r$ is increasing, the value at the left end of each subinterval is the least on that subinterval, so each rectangle lies under the graph and 65 is an underestimate.
earns.why: It uses the unequal widths, writes the sum before the number, and ties the conclusion to $r$ increasing.

misses.answer: $3(4 + 7 + 9) = 60$ liters, an underestimate because it is a left sum.
misses.why: The widths are 2, 3 and 4, not 3 each. And "left sum" is not a reason: a left sum overestimates a decreasing function. The reason is that $r$ is increasing.

prompts.title: What an integral of a rate means
prompts.context: Cars pass a toll booth at the rate $R(t)$ cars per minute, $t$ minutes after 8 a.m. $\int_2^8 R(t)\,dt = 45$.
prompts.prompt: Interpret $\int_2^8 R(t)\,dt = 45$ in the context of the problem, with units.
checklist: Names the quantity: the number of cars that pass the booth
Names the time interval: from $t = 2$ to $t = 8$ minutes (8:02 to 8:08 a.m.)
Gives the unit of the accumulated amount, cars, not cars per minute

earns.answer: 45 cars pass the toll booth between $t = 2$ and $t = 8$ minutes after 8 a.m., that is, from 8:02 to 8:08.
earns.why: Quantity, interval and units are all there; the integral of a rate is the amount that builds up.

misses.answer: The rate of cars passing the booth is 45 cars per minute.
misses.why: The integral of a rate is not a rate. It is the number of cars over an interval, and the answer names no interval.

prompts.title: An extremum of an accumulation function
prompts.context: The function $f$ is continuous, with $f(t) > 0$ on $(0, 3)$ and $f(t) < 0$ on $(3, 7)$. Let $g(x) = \int_0^x f(t)\,dt$.
prompts.prompt: Does $g$ have a relative maximum, a relative minimum, or neither at $x = 3$? Justify your answer.
checklist: Says $g' = f$ changes from positive to negative at $x = 3$
Concludes $g$ has a relative maximum at $x = 3$

earns.answer: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, $g'(x) = f(x)$. $g' = f$ changes from positive to negative at $x = 3$, so $g$ has a relative maximum at $x = 3$.
earns.why: It names the function that changes sign ($g'$, which is $f$) and the direction of the change.

misses.answer: $g$ has a relative maximum at $x = 3$ because $f(3) = 0$ and the graph of $f$ crosses the axis there.
misses.why: The reason is the sign change of $g'$; "$f(3) = 0$" alone fits a minimum too, and "the graph crosses" does not say which function or in which direction.

prompts.title: When the upper limit is below the lower
prompts.context: Let $g(x) = 5 + \int_4^x f(t)\,dt$, where $f$ is continuous and $\int_1^4 f(t)\,dt = 6$.
prompts.prompt: Find $g(1)$. Show the work that leads to your answer.
checklist: Keeps the starting value 5 and gets $g(1) = 5 - 6 = -1$

earns.why: It keeps the starting value 5 and changes the sign when the limits are reversed.

misses.why: The integral in $g(1)$ runs from 4 down to 1, so it is the negative of $\int_1^4 f(t)\,dt$. Swapping the limits without changing the sign gives the wrong value.
